properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
properties.digitization_method: SPLIT 2026-09-16 from the combined blklot 4046001 row (see Building 101's digitization_method for the full context of that split). Matched to this building using the same method: Figure 6.4.2's own '102' label position, transformed via this site's validated 6-point affine transform, matched to the nearest real footprint in the lot (23.2m away -- clearly the best match; the next-nearest candidate was over 70m away). Confirmed spatially distinct from Building 101's own footprint (which ends about 88m to the west) rather than one merged structure, despite the two being described as closely adjacent (a 2013 HPC packet notes 'an access ramp or stairs would be provided between Buildings 101 and 102 to navigate the grade change'). This is a REAL surveyed building outline, not a diagram trace. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: blklot 4046001, named as the lot holding this building's footprint, is not a current Assessor lot: DataSF retired it on 2018-10-02 (acdm-wktn; active=false) and the footprint now falls within active lot 3941041 (no street address). The lot reference above reflects the 2013 HPC packet's 'Block 4046, Lot 001'. Nothing in the geometry was changed.
properties.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself. CORRECTED 2026-09-29: this footprint's area (~1955 m2 / ~21,043 sqft) does not match the building. The National Register nomination gives Building 102's dimensions as 128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in (about 5,440 sqft, ~505 m2 as a rectangle), so this outline is roughly four times the building's own footprint and probably includes neighboring structures or other area; the '11,266 sf' Port figure is not the likely source of the discrepancy. The geometry is signed off and was not changed; the outline should not be read as the building's own footprint.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: The former Assessor lot blklot 4046001 (which held Buildings 101, 102, 104 and 122/123 in the 2013 HPC packet) was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, active=false); in DataSF's current layer this footprint falls within active lot 3941041, which has no street address. No cited source ties the building to a current lot, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
properties.regulatory_context: The former Power House, built 1912, part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as Building 101 (HPC packet 2013.1168E, Nov 26 2013 review). Per that packet, Building 102 was 'in fairly good condition' at the time and in use as the powerhouse facility. Port Item 12A (memo dated Jan 4, 2019) names JUUL Labs as the ten-year sublessee of the entire building less the Port's basement electrical equipment room, and Potrero View (Mar 2019) says JUUL 'sublets offices in Building 102'; no source after 2020 confirms a current occupant.
properties.notes: Split 2026-09-16 from the combined 'Historic Core, north side' entry -- see digitization_method and accuracy_caveat (sqft discrepancy). Status 'complete' is supported by Retrofit magazine's Nov 9, 2020 profile of the finished rehabilitation (no completion date given); the 2013 HPC packet cited for the geometry only proposed the work.
